Successful publication retains its exact bytes after new-instance recovery
Recovery follows the old publisher's committed task and saved index
Late old-instance updates cannot restore a deleted task or saved file
Cancelled writer permits a new main-thread constructor while retaining its URI lease
Cancelled writer permits another main-thread message before lease release
Cancelled publication removes its bytes before the waiting recovery inspects them
Waiting recovery never records an aborted destination as saved
An abandoned incomplete destination is cleaned without inventing a saved record
A published orphan is recovered only after its real destination exists
A late failed-save callback cannot clear a newer destination and generation
An older save generation cannot commit after task replacement
Conflicting stale task edits preserve the newer durable row
Saving one instance preserves tasks added by another instance
The direct recovery API rejects main-thread file-lock acquisition
Publication rejects main-thread lease acquisition instead of waiting for itself
A live older download without a pending destination is not marked interrupted
A second instance cannot take over a still-live owner by selecting its task
An unchanged local merge retains the running task object and later real progress
After its owner ends an interrupted task is recovered without retaining a live writer

Recovery retries rejected metadata before confirming the retained published bytes
Index failure after durable saved metadata cannot abort or downgrade publication

A new instance ignores failed cached saved and explicitly commits recovery
Only a confirmed recovery receipt permits source cleanup and completion
Equal cached rows never bypass a new instance's unconfirmed write retry
A new empty instance also retries equal rows after failed persistence
Pending recovery returns the replacement row when destination is missing
Recovered failed row can be claimed and saved in a new generation
Equivalent reordered JSON retains the running task object

scope: Production Java download task/recovery/publication/deletion methods and real host files/locks. Android main queue, preferences with independent memory/disk, local URI provider and index are explicit doubles. Includes failures before memory, after memory before disk, post-commit index failure, completion/source-cleanup gate and two separate JVM processes loading persisted fixture disk. No Android durability, physical-device or latency evidence.
